H1410H.name: Gad
H1410H.desc: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
H1410H.brief: Prophet during the reigns of David and Solomon.
H1410H.short: Gad was a prophet who advised King David and wrote a book of his acts.

H1410G.name: Gad
H1410G.desc: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
H1410G.brief: Israelite tribe; descended from Gad, son of Jacob.
H1410G.short: Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel, descended from Gad, the son of Jacob, and known for their military prowess and settlement east of the Jordan River.

H1426.name: Gaddi
H1426.desc: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H1426.brief: Son of Susi; representative of Manasseh among the spies.
H1426.short: Gaddi, the son of Susi, was the representative of the tribe of Manasseh among the twelve spies sent to explore Canaan.

H1427.name: Gaddiel
H1427.desc: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H1427.brief: Son of Sodi; representative of Zebulun among the spies.
H1427.short: Gaddiel, the son of Sodi, was the representative of the tribe of Zebulun among the twelve spies sent to explore Canaan.

H1424.name: Gadi
H1424.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H1424.brief: Father of Menahem, king of Israel.
H1424.short: Gadi was the father of Menahem, who became king of Israel after assassinating Shallum.

H1495G.name: Gazez
H1495G.desc: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H1495G.brief: Son of Caleb and his concubine Ephah.
H1495G.short: Gazez was a son of Caleb and his concubine Ephah, born after Haran.

H1495H.name: Gazez
H1495H.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H1495H.short: Gazez was a grandson of Caleb, born to Haran's son Gazez.

H1436I.name: Gedaliah
H1436I.desc: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
H1436I.brief: Son of Jeduthun; a temple musician during David's reign.
H1436I.short: Gedaliah, a son of Jeduthun, was one of the temple musicians appointed by King David to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals.

H1436B.name: Gedaliah
H1436B.desc: Governor living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H1436B.brief: Appointed governor of Judah by Babylonians; assassinated by Ishmael.
H1436B.short: Gedaliah, appointed governor of Judah by the Babylonians after the fall of Jerusalem, was assassinated by Ishmael, leading to the flight of the remaining Jews to Egypt.

H1436A.name: Gedaliah
H1436A.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H1436A.brief: Priest who married a foreign woman during the Exile.
H1436A.short: Gedaliah, a priest, was among those who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile and pledged to put them away.

H1436J.name: Gedaliah
H1436J.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H1436J.brief: Son of Pashhur; an official during Zedekiah's reign.
H1436J.short: Gedaliah, the son of Pashhur, was one of the officials who heard Jeremiah's message and urged King Zedekiah to put him to death.

H1436H.name: Gedaliah
H1436H.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H1436H.short: Gedaliah was the grandfather of the prophet Zephaniah, who prophesied during the reign of King Josiah of Judah.

H1446I.name: Gedor
H1446I.desc: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
H1446I.brief: Son of Abiel, the founder of Gibeon.
H1446I.short: Gedor was a son of Abiel (or 'Jeiel'), the  father (ie re-founder) of Gibeon, and an ancestor of King Saul.

H1437.name: Giddalti
H1437.desc: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H1437.brief: Son of Heman; a temple musician during David's reign.
H1437.short: Giddalti was one of the sons of Heman, appointed by King David as a temple musician to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals.

H1435G.name: Giddel
H1435G.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H1435G.brief: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
H1435G.short: Giddel was an ancestor of a group of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.

H1435H.name: Giddel
H1435H.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H1435H.brief: Ancestor of Solomon's servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
H1435H.short: Giddel was an ancestor of a group of Solomon's servants who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.

H1439.name: Gideon
H1439.brief: Judge of Israel; defeated Midianites; tested and reassured by God.
H1439.short: Gideon, also called Jerubbaal or Jerubbesheth, was a judge of Israel who, with God's help, defeated the Midianites and delivered Israel from oppression.

H1441.name: Gideoni
H1441.desc: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H1441.brief: Leader of the tribe of Benjamin during the Exodus.
H1441.short: Gideoni, the son of Abidan, was the leader of the tribe of Benjamin during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness.

H1493.name: Gizonites
H1493.brief: A people group mentioned in the Old Testament.
H1493.short: The Gizonites are mentioned in <ref="1Ch.11.34">1Ch.11.34</ref> without any additional context.

H1463G.name: Gog
H1463G.desc: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H1463G.brief: A descendant of Reuben, son of Joel.
H1463G.short: Gog, a descendant of Reuben, is mentioned in the genealogy of Reuben in <ref="1Ch.5.4">1Ch.5.4</ref>.

H1471B.name: Goiim
H1471B.brief: A king of Goyim who fought alongside Chedorlaomer.
H1471B.short: Tidal, king of Goiim (nations), was one of the kings who fought alongside Chedorlaomer in Genesis 14.

H1476H.name: Guni
H1476H.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H1476H.brief: A descendant of Gad; father of Abdiel.
H1476H.short: Guni, a descendant of Gad, was the father of Abdiel, as mentioned in the genealogy of Gad.

H1476G.name: Guni
H1476G.desc: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H1476G.brief: Son of Naphtali, grandson of Jacob.
H1476G.short: Guni was a son of Naphtali and a grandson of Jacob, as listed in the genealogies of Genesis and Numbers.

H1419B.name: Haggedolim
H1419B.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H1419B.brief: A priest mentioned in Nehemiah's time.
H1419B.short: Haggedolim was a priest during the time of Nehemiah, mentioned in the list of priests and Levites.

H1449.name: Gederah
H1449.brief: Town in Judah; home of Baal-hanan and Jozabad
H1449.short: Gederah, a town in Judah, was the home of Baal-hanan, one of David's overseers, and Jozabad, one of his mighty men.

H1450.name: Gederoth
H1450.brief: Town in Judah; captured by Philistines during Ahaz's reign
H1450.short: Gederoth, a town in Judah, was captured by the Philistines during the reign of King Ahaz.

H1453.name: Gederothaim
H1453.brief: Town in Judah; mentioned in list of allotted cities
H1453.short: Gederothaim, a town in Judah, is mentioned in the list of cities allotted to the tribe of Judah.

H1446H.name: Gedor
H1446H.brief: Region where Simeonites sought pasture for their flocks
H1446H.short: Gedor, a region where some Simeonites went to find pasture for their flocks during the reign of King Hezekiah.

H1446G.name: Gedor
H1446G.brief: Town in Judah; home of Judahite clan members
H1446G.short: Gedor (or Geder), a town in the hill country of Judah, was the home of several members of Judahite clans.

H1405.name: Gibbethon
H1405.brief: A Levitical city in the territory of Dan.
H1405.short: Gibbethon, a Levitical city in the territory of Dan, was the site of conflict during the reigns of Nadab and Baasha (<ref="Joshua 19:44; 21:23; 1Ki.15.27; 16:15, 17">Joshua 19:44; 21:23; 1Ki.15.27; 16:15, 17</ref>).

H1440.name: Gidom
H1440.brief: A place near Gibeah, associated with the Benjamite War.
H1440.short: Gidom was a place near Gibeah where the Benjamites were pursued and defeated during the Benjamite War (<ref="Judges 20:45">Judges 20:45</ref>).

H1463H.name: Gog
H1463H.brief: A symbolic enemy of God's people in prophetic literature.
H1463H.short: Gog is mentioned in the prophetic books of Ezekiel and Revelation as a symbolic enemy of God's people who will be defeated in the end times (<ref="Ezk.38.2, 3, 14, 16, 18; 39:1, 11; Revelation 20:8">Ezk.38.2, 3, 14, 16, 18; 39:1, 11; Revelation 20:8</ref>).

H1474.name: Golan
H1474.brief: A city of refuge in Bashan, allotted to Manasseh.
H1474.short: Golan was a city of refuge in Bashan, allotted to the Levites of the family of Gershon and located in the territory of the half-tribe of Manasseh (<ref="Deu.4.43; Joshua 20:8; 21:27; 1Ch.6.71">Deu.4.43; Joshua 20:8; 21:27; 1Ch.6.71</ref>).

H1470.name: Gozan
H1470.brief: A region in Mesopotamia where Israelite captives were deported.
H1470.short: Gozan was a region in Mesopotamia where Israelite captives from the northern kingdom were deported by the Assyrians (<ref="2Ki.17.6; 18:11; 19:12; 1Ch.5.26; Isaiah 37:12">2Ki.17.6; 18:11; 19:12; 1Ch.5.26; Isaiah 37:12</ref>).

H1419J.name: Great Sea
H1419J.brief: The Mediterranean Sea, the western boundary of the Promised Land.
H1419J.short: The Great Sea, also known as the Sea of the Philistines, refers to the Mediterranean Sea, which formed the western boundary of the Promised Land (<ref="Numbers 34:6-7; Joshua 1:4; 9:1; 15:12, 47; 23:4; Ezk.47.10, 15, 19-20; 48:28; Exodus 23:31">Numbers 34:6-7; Joshua 1:4; 9:1; 15:12, 47; 23:4; Ezk.47.10, 15, 19-20; 48:28; Exodus 23:31</ref>).

H1483.name: Gur
H1483.brief: A place near Ibleam where Ahaziah was wounded.
H1483.short: Gur was a place near Ibleam where Ahaziah, king of Judah, was wounded by Jehu's men while fleeing (<ref="2Ki.9.27">2Ki.9.27</ref>).

H1485.name: Gurbaal
H1485.brief: A place inhabited by Arabians, attacked by Uzziah's army.
H1485.short: Gurbaal was a place inhabited by Arabians, against whom Uzziah, king of Judah, waged war and prevailed (<ref="2Ch.26.7">2Ch.26.7</ref>).

H1408.name: Fortune
H1408.brief: A pagan deity associated with luck and prosperity
H1408.short: Fortune, mentioned in <ref="Isaiah 65:11">Isaiah 65:11</ref>, is a pagan deity associated with luck and prosperity, which some Israelites worshipped, forsaking the Lord.

H1403.name: Gabriel
H1403.brief: An angel who delivers messages from God
H1403.short: Gabriel is an angel who appears in the Bible to deliver important messages from God, such as interpreting visions for Daniel (<ref="Dan.8.16; 9:21">Dan.8.16; 9:21</ref>) and announcing the births of John the Baptist and Jesus (<ref="Luke 1:19, 26">Luke 1:19, 26</ref>).
